blocks.value: An enum (enumeration) is a data type that holds a fixed set of constants, useful whenever you already know every possible value ahead of time, like compass directions, months of the year, or cards in a deck. Unlike numeric or String constants, an enum makes it impossible to assign an invalid value without triggering a compiler error.
Declare one with the enum keyword, a type name, and a list of allowed values called enum constants:
Once declared, you can use it just like any other type:
An enum type is actually a class, and its constants behave like objects of that class, complete with built-in (non-static) methods. Given p = Period.MIDTERM:

Method        Description                                             Example
toString()    the constant's name as a String                        p.toString() is "MIDTERM"
ordinal()     the constant's position in the list, starting at 0     p.ordinal() is 1
equals()      true if the argument equals this constant              p.equals(Period.PRELIM) is false
compareTo()   negative/0/positive based on ordinal position          p.compareTo(Period.FINAL) is negative
